content_sections.title: Every day and yesterday
content_sections.body_text: Read: ‘Every day, I run home after class.’ Read: ‘Yesterday, I ran to the bus stop.’ Run is for the routine; ran is for the past action. Cover the lines, write them, and check the first word and the verb together.

content_sections.title: Count the beats
content_sections.body_text: Tap once for run and home, twice for af-ter, and twice for ad-dress. Say each word slowly, then at normal speed. Do not add a new sound at the end. Record both speeds and tap while you replay; the number of taps must stay the same.

content_sections.title: Ask someone to write it down
content_sections.body_text: Mai: ‘Please help me write my address on this form.’ An: ‘Yes. Tell me the address.’ Mai: ‘12 Park Road.’ An: ‘I’ll write it down here.’ Read both roles. An is the writer, so the answer fits the request. Use a made-up address for practice.

content_sections.title: Use all four skills
content_sections.body_text: Write one routine and one past action with run/ran. Add the address dialogue. Record both roles with pauses, hide your text, and replay. Write down the routine, past time, and address that you hear; then compare with your script. Say the dialogue once more and answer each pause before reading the next line.
